answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by bonding collateral into a shared stake: every new identity must lock real value that gets slashed if it acts fraudulently. To spin up a fake ocean of identities, an attacker must multiply that locked stake, so the cost scales with each clone. Once fraud is detected it triggers a spiral of forfeited bonds, and the hard basalt floor of required stake ensures every extra fake identity burns genuine capital, making the attack unprofitable.
